design-tokens-getting-started--docs.title: Design Tokens/Getting Started
design-tokens-getting-started--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

Design Tokens

Our design system is powered by design tokens: name-value pairs that define the visual language of Infomaniak products. Tokens ensure consistency across platforms while remaining flexible enough for different contexts.

- [Token Architecture](#token-architecture) - [Consuming Tokens](#consuming-tokens) - [Web](#web) - [Install from NPM](#install-from-npm) - [CSS Files](#css-files) - [Loading Themes (.root files)](#loading-themes-root-files) - [Using Modifiers (.attr files)](#using-modifiers-attr-files) - [Tailwind CSS](#tailwind-css) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Token Resolution Chain](#token-resolution-chain) - [Modifiers Override by Path Matching](#modifiers-override-by-path-matching) ## Token Architecture Our token system follows the Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) standard with a three-tier architecture: - T1 Primitive tokens for foundational tokens values - T2 Semantic tokens for semantic abstraction tokens - T3 Component tokens for component-specific tokens ## Consuming Tokens ### Web #### Install from NPM ```bash npm install @infomaniak-design-system/tokens ``` #### CSS Files We offer two CSS file formats: *.root.css, :root, :host,

*.root.css files apply globally via :root immediately.
Use media queries with theme files to prevent conflicts (e.g., loading both light and dark simultaneously).

, ], [ *.attr.css, [data-esds-<modifier>="<context>"],

.attr.css files only affect elements inside a container with the matching data attribute.

  • <modifier>: "theme" | "product"
  • <context>: "infomaniak" | "mail" | "euria" | ...
, ], ]} /> #### Using `*.root.css` files Root CSS files could be loaded using query, for example: ```html ``` #### Using `*.attr.css` files Attr CSS file could be imported via CSS and activated using data attributes: **NOTE**: `*.attr.css` CSS files are **optional** and should be imported only if necessary. ```css @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/tokens.attr.css'; @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/product/mail.attr.css'; @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/modifiers/theme/dark.attr.css'; ``` Modifiers can also be set on container elements: ```html ``` #### Tailwind CSS ```css @import 'tailwindcss'; @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/css/tokens.root.css'; @import '@infomaniak-design-system/tokens/tailwind.css'; ``` ```html ``` ## How It Works ### Token Resolution Chain Token values reference each other in a hierarchy, ensuring consistency across the system: ``` T3-Component → button.background.error ↓ T2-Semantic → color.background.error.default ↓ T1-Primitive → color.red.600 (#E21C40) ``` When a primitive value changes, every token referencing it updates automatically. ### Modifiers Override by Path Matching Modifiers let you swap the values of existing tokens without changing their names. They work by matching the path of a T2 (semantic) or T3 (component) token and replacing its value for specific contexts. **How it works:** 1. A modifier file contains the same token path as the base token 2. When applied, it replaces that path's value in the CSS cascade 3. Resolution continues with the new value **Example**: The `euria` product modifier The `euria.tokens.json` modifier overrides `color.background.brand.default` by including the same path with a different value: Base `t2-semantic/color.tokens.json`: ```json { "color": { "background": { "brand": { "default": { "$value": "{color.sky.700}" } } } } } ``` `modifiers/product/euria.tokens.json`: ```json { "color": { "background": { "brand": { "default": { "$value": "{color.ocean.700}" } } } } } ``` **Resolution with modifiers:** Multiple modifiers can be applied simultaneously. In the example below, the `euria` modifier changes the base brand color, then `dark` further adjusts it for the dark theme: ``` With data-esds-product="euria" data-esds-theme="dark": T3: button.background.brand.default ↓ T2: color.background.brand.default ↓ Euria modifier: color.background.brand.default (color.ocean.700) ↓ Dark modifier: color.background.brand.default (color.ocean.400) ↓ T1: color.ocean.400 ``` **Apply modifiers using data attributes:** ```html ```

design-tokens-t1--docs.content: import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; # T1 Primitive Tokens ## What are T1 Tokens? T1 tokens are the foundational design tokens that define the raw values of your design system. These are the base values that don't reference other tokens. ### Characteristics: - **Base values**: Colors, spacing, shadows, etc. - **No references**: They contain actual values (hex colors, pixel dimensions) - **Platform agnostic**: Represent the design intent without assumptions about usage - **Source of truth**: Other tiers reference these values ### Token Categories in T1: Blur, 'Background blur effects'], [ Border Width, 'Border thickness values', ], [Breakpoint, 'Responsive breakpoints'], [Color, 'Color palette'], [Font, 'Typography tokens'], [Opacity, 'Opacity values'], [Radius, 'Border radius values'], [Ratio, 'Aspect ratios'], [Scale, 'Scaling values'], [Shadow, 'Shadow effects'], [Spacing, 'Spacing scale'], ]} />

design-tokens-t2--docs.content: import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; # T2 Semantic Tokens ## What are T2 Tokens? T2 tokens are semantic design tokens that reference T1 (primitive) values. They define aliases and common names to abstract the T1 tokens. ### Characteristics: - **Purpose-driven naming**: Named by what they do, not what they are - **Resolve to T1 values**: Point to primitive tokens for actual values - **Modifiers**: Modifiers could override T2 tokens to adapt to a specific use cases - **Cross-component usage**: Used by multiple components - **Design patterns**: Semantic layer ensures consistent usage ### Examples: - `color.background.primary` instead of `color.blue.500` - `spacing.section.large` instead of `spacing.32` ### Token Categories in T2: Border, 'Semantic border styles', ], [ Color, 'Semantic color aliases', ], [Font, 'Semantic typography'], [Icon, 'Icon-related tokens'], [ Radius, 'Semantic border radius', ], [ Spacing, 'Semantic spacing', ], [Text, 'Text styling tokens'], ]} />

design-tokens-t3--docs.content: import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; # T3 Component Tokens ## What are T3 Tokens? T3 tokens are component-specific design tokens that reference T1 (primitive) and T2 (semantic) values. They define visual properties for specific components. ### Characteristics: - **Component-specific**: Named after a specific component - **Reference T1 and T2**: Points to lower tier tokens - **Modifiers**: Modifiers could override T3 tokens to adapt to a specific use cases - **Single component usage**: Used by one specific component - **Different variants**: Supports component states (hover, active, disabled) ### Examples: - `button.background.hover` using `color.background.primary.hover` - `card.padding` using `spacing.section.medium` ### Token Categories in T3: Typography, 'Typography component styles', ], ]} />

icons-icon-component--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; # Web ## EsdsIconComponent ### Installation ```shell yarn add @infomaniak-design-system/esds-icon ``` ### Initialization The icon component needs to be initialized before it can be rendered: ```ts import { EsdsIconComponent } from '@infomaniak-design-system/esds-icon'; EsdsIconComponent.init(); ``` This allows defining the API proxy to fetch the icons and registering the custom element. You should put it in your `main.ts` or `app.ts` file. ### Usage ```html ``` #### Styling The icon may be styled using the following CSS properties: - `color`: to set the icon's color - `font-size`: to set the icon's size ### API
Attribute/Property Type Description
name <prefix>:<name> The name of the icon to display.
mode EsdsIconComponentMode The mode to apply:
  • svg: injects the svg as direct <svg> child of this component.
  • bg: uses the svg as "background-image" of this component.
  • mask: injects the svg as "mask-image" of this component: this is useful to apply color to the svg.
inline boolean Adding inline property to the icon component is identical to setting{' '} style="vertical-align: -0.125em". This is useful to correct the icon's alignment.
nolazy boolean By default, icons are rendered only when visible to the visitor. You can opt out of this behavior by adding the nolazy attribute.
